To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the corrosion rate of the implanted samples was lower than that of the un-implanted samples, and (2) there was a strong correlation between the corrosion resistance and the surface layer structure.
the corrosion resistance of iron, stainless steel, and medium carbon steel can be enhanced by multi-element ion implantations.

the corrosion resistance of stainless steel, pure iron and chromium-depositated iron can be enhanced significantly by implanting with Cu, Mo, Ni or Yb, and that the corrosion behavior is influenced strongly by the dose, energy, and combination of implanted species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of ion implantation of various elements into stainless steel, medium-carbon steel, and pure iron.
the influence of multi-element ion-beam bombardment on the electrochemical corrosion resistance of stainless steel and iron.
the effect of ion beam implantation of various metals on the corrosion resistance of stainless steel, medium-carbon steel, and chromium-deposit-iron to acid solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ion implantation of a variety of metals and alloys, with a variety of ions, at various ion energies and doses, can improve the corrosion resistance of iron, steel and stainless steel.
, in the case of the present experiments, ion implantation with the selected elements and doses does not improve the corrosion resistance of iron and steel to acid solutions.
multi-element ion beam mixing is an extremely effective method of producing surface layers with improved corrosion properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ion bombardment with the above elements can increase the corrosion resistance of iron and steel, especially for stainless steel and medium carbon steel, and the effect is most marked for the elements Cr, Mo, and Ni.

the corrosion behavior of ion-implanted samples can be described in terms of the chemical and physical properties of the surface layer, and that the corrosion resistance can be increased by the appropriate combination of ion species and dose.
ion beam bombardment can improve the corrosion resistance of stainless steel and pure iron.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ion implantation can be used to modify the corrosion behavior of stainless steel and medium carbon steel in acid environments.
the corrosion resistance of the implanted samples is strongly influenced by the composition and structure in the near surface region.
the ion implantation process is a very effective method of improving the corrosion resistance of iron and steel.
